item.title: The seven programming ur-languages (2022)
item.description:
📝 The ur-languages are: ALGOL Lisp ML Self Forth APL Prolog ALGOL Characteristics. Most common programming languages trace to this ur-language. ALGOL itself included ALGOL 58, ALGOL 60, ALGOL W, and ALGOL 68.
🔗 Read more: https://madhadron.com/programming/seven_ur_languages.html

item.title: Show HN: Prompt-to-Excalidraw demo with Gemma 4 E2B in the browser (3.1GB)
item.description:

🔗 Read more: https://teamchong.github.io/turboquant-wasm/draw.html

item.title: Binary GCD
item.description:
📝 The textbook also probably mentioned that the worst possible input to Euclid’s algorithm — the one that maximizes the total number of steps — are consecutive Fibonacci numbers, and since they grow exponentially, the running time of the algorithm is logarithmic in the worst case. Likewise, the algorithm itself is just a repeated application of these identities. What makes this algorithm especially interesting to us is that the only arithmetic operations it uses are binary shifts, comparisons, and subtractions, all of which typically take just one cycle.
🔗 Read more: https://en.algorithmica.org/hpc/algorithms/gcd/#binary-gcd
